_notes.owner: The name the shelf is called by: "Robin" makes it Robin's shelf.
_notes.theme: The room's look: "library" (green walls, oak, warm lamplight), "studio" (cool white and slate), or "paper" (bright paper and indigo ink). Each has a daylight and a lamplight version that follows the device, with a switch on the page.
_notes.openLibrary: true lets the page find covers on Open Library for books that have none, as the shelf comes into view. The sample keeps it false so it shows with no network.
_notes.books: One entry per book, in the order they stand on the shelf.
_notes.books[].title: The title. Required.
_notes.books[].author: The author. Required.
_notes.books[].isbn: The ISBN, when known; it finds the right cover on Open Library.
_notes.books[].status: "read", "reading", or "want". Books being read stand face-out with a bookmark.
_notes.books[].note: A line or two in the person's own words, set inside the book when it opens.
_notes.books[].finished: The day it was finished, as 2026-03-14. Finished books fill the stats.
_notes.books[].pages: The page count; it sets how thick the book is on the shelf.
_notes.books[].page: For a book being read, the page the bookmark is on.
_notes.books[].cover: A cover image beside this file, as covers/moby-dick.jpg. Leave it out to use Open Library or a cover drawn in the theme's colors.

books.title: Middlemarch
books.author: George Eliot
books.note: Dorothea deserves so much better than Casaubon, and Eliot knows it. A chapter a night before bed.

books.title: Moby-Dick
books.author: Herman Melville
books.note: Skipped nothing, not even the chapters on whale anatomy, and I'm glad. Ishmael is the best company on a long voyage.

books.title: The Great Gatsby
books.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
books.note: Gorgeous sentences, hollow people. Which I think is the point.

books.title: Frankenstein
books.author: Mary Shelley
books.note: The creature is the most articulate person in the book. Read it over two stormy evenings.

books.title: Pride and Prejudice
books.author: Jane Austen
books.note: Fourth time through. The proposal at Hunsford still makes me wince and grin at once.

books.title: To the Lighthouse
books.author: Virginia Woolf
books.note: Slower than Dalloway. The middle section, Time Passes, floored me.

books.title: The Odyssey
books.author: Homer
books.note: Fagles makes it move like a thriller. The homecoming in book twenty-two is brutal.

books.title: Mrs. Dalloway
books.author: Virginia Woolf
books.note: One June day in London, and somehow a whole life. Read it in a single sitting.

books.title: Dracula
books.author: Bram Stoker
books.note: Told in letters and diaries, so the dread creeps in sideways. Perfect for October.

books.title: Anna Karenina
books.author: Leo Tolstoy
books.note: Saving this one for the first snow, with a pot of tea.
